analysis: Single added file: provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live/PrefixQualification/ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift (opt-in live benchmark test, gated by DARKBLOOM_RESTORE_CONTENTION_BENCHMARK=1, requires an absolute new output path and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_EXCLUSIVE_GPU=1). No production source is changed, so there is no new runtime attack surface or change to the TB-002/TB-007/TB-011 controls. Relevant to T-041 (prefix-cache SSD tier and TTFT oracle): the test exercises SSD checkpoint restore with per-condition tenant scopes ("contention-<pair>-<condition>" and a distinct foreign scope), so it checks cross-scope isolation only indirectly. It does not weaken or alter the scope derivation, HMAC lookup tags, TTL or disk budget. The report JSON (Report.save) holds only the model ID, weight hash, timing and token counts, with no prompt content, keys or plaintext tokens. The test uses synthetic prompts from ModelCheckpointStoragePrompts, which is outside the supplied evidence; the fixture, session and benchmark helpers (ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture, drainCheckpointWrites) are not supplied. It uses the @_spi(Benchmarking) @testable import, so SPI exposure is test-only as far as the evidence shows; whether the SPI is compiled into production binaries is unverified, and it is not a PR change in this file. The output write uses .atomic with a new absolute path and a pre-check for non-existence, which is a minor TOCTOU in test code only, not a security finding. No findings.
